40 The nuclei of common isotopes of hydrogen, helium, lithium and beryllium are shown.
Which nucleus contains equal numbers of up and down quarks?
A
1
1H
B
4
2He
C
7
3Li
D
9
4Be

hints: Recall the quark make-up of the nucleons in the $^{A}_{Z}\text{X}$ nuclei: proton is $uud$ and neutron is $udd$.
Count protons as $Z$ and neutrons as $A-Z$ for each of the four given isotopes, then work out total up quarks as $2Z + 1(A-Z)$ and total down quarks as $1Z + 2(A-Z)$.
Set total up equal to total down and check which isotope satisfies $A = 2Z$, meaning equal proton and neutron numbers.
walkthrough: Read $^{A}_{Z}\text{X}$ as $Z$ protons and $N = A-Z$ neutrons. So $^{1}_{1}\text{H}$ is 1p + 0n, $^{4}_{2}\text{He}$ is 2p + 2n, $^{7}_{3}\text{Li}$ is 3p + 4n, $^{9}_{4}\text{Be}$ is 4p + 5n.
State the quark rule: proton $= uud$ gives 2 up and 1 down, neutron $= udd$ gives 1 up and 2 down.
For a nucleus with $Z$ protons and $N$ neutrons, total up $= 2Z + N$ and total down $= Z + 2N$.
Equal numbers requires $2Z + N = Z + 2N$, which simplifies to $Z = N$, or $A = 2Z$.
Only $^{4}_{2}\text{He}$ has $Z = 2$ and $N = 4-2 = 2$. Its totals are up $= 2(2)+2 = 6$ and down $= 2+2(2) = 6$.
The other nuclei have more neutrons than protons, so down quarks outnumber up quarks. This is option B.

A.explanation: $^{1}_{1}\text{H}$ is one proton with quark content $uud$, giving 2 up quarks and 1 down quark, so they are not equal.

B.explanation: $^{4}_{2}\text{He}$ has 2 protons and 2 neutrons, giving total up $=6$ and total down $=6$, so the numbers are equal.

C.explanation: $^{7}_{3}\text{Li}$ has 3 protons and 4 neutrons, giving 10 up quarks and 11 down quarks, so down quarks exceed up quarks.

D.explanation: $^{9}_{4}\text{Be}$ has 4 protons and 5 neutrons, giving 13 up quarks and 14 down quarks, so down quarks exceed up quarks.
